candidate_profile.description: The candidate correctly structures the route acquisition as a profitability decision and includes the main revenue, cost, and cannibalization drivers, though the synthesis is more solid than exceptional.
behaviour_rules: Open with a clear recap and frame the route as an incremental profitability question.
Use a workable structure covering revenues, costs, competition, and cannibalization.
Identify occupancy rates and ticket prices as the two core revenue levers.
Recognize that demand and competitive dynamics determine those revenue levers.
Identify fuel and landing rights as key operating costs.
Include cannibalization of Tokyo-LA and LA-New York routes in the analysis.
Recognize that stealing passengers from the airline's own routes may still be better than losing them to competitors.
Recommend acquiring the route only if incremental revenue exceeds incremental operating cost plus net cannibalization effects.

expected_issues: Covers the right factors, but may not prioritize them especially sharply.
Cannibalization logic is correct but may not be discussed with much strategic nuance.
Recommendation is sound, though not especially board-ready.
expected_feedback_points: Good identification of occupancy, pricing, and competition as revenue drivers.
Good inclusion of fuel, landing rights, and cannibalization in the cost side.
Correct recognition that self-cannibalization can still be strategically preferable to losing traffic to rivals.
Reasonable recommendation based on positive net incremental economics.
